title: Cyber insurance claims - what policies actually cover
p1:
Think cyber insurance pays for every cyber attack? That assumption can become a costly surprise.

Many businesses buy a policy after hearing about data breaches, but discover later that coverage depends on what actually happened and what protection they purchased.
p2:
A common misconception is that cyber insurance is like a blanket safety net. It usually does not cover every loss caused by a hacker.

Some policies may cover costs like investigating a breach, notifying affected customers, recovering data, legal expenses, or business interruption losses. But exclusions, security requirements, and policy limits can decide whether a claim succeeds.
p3:
The surprising part: even having insurance may not be enough if basic security measures were ignored. Insurers often check whether companies followed required safeguards before approving claims.

The practical takeaway? Cyber insurance works best when combined with strong security practices, not as a replacement for them.
conclusion: Have you ever reviewed what your cyber insurance policy actually covers before needing to make a claim?
